result.stdout:
Usage: squeeze [options] [file...]

Compress and decompress files using gzip, brotli, or zstd.

Options:
  -d, --decompress             Decompress (auto-detects format)
  -b, --brotli                 Use brotli format
  -z, --zstd                   Use zstd format
  -c, --stdout                 Write to stdout
  -f, --force                  Overwrite existing output files
  --remove                     Delete input file after success
  -k, --keep                   Keep original file (default; takes precedence if --remove also set)
  -v, --verbose                Show stats even when piped
  -q, --quiet                  Suppress stats even on terminal
  --level N                    Compression level (format-specific range)
  -o, --output FILE            Output file (single input only)
  -h, --help                   Show help
  --version                    Show version
  --no-color                   Disable colored output
  --json                       JSON output
  --describe                   Structured JSON metadata for AI agents
  --color[=auto|always|never]  Coloured output: auto (default when omitted), always, or never

Compatibility:
  These flags match gzip for muscle memory:
  -d                  Same as --decompress
  -c                  Same as --stdout
  -k                  Keep input (precedence over --remove if both set)
  -1..-9              Same as --level 1..9
  -v                  Same as --verbose
  -f                  Same as --force

Wildcards (Windows):
  On Windows, * and ? in path arguments are expanded by squeeze itself
  (cmd and PowerShell don't expand them). [...] is matched literally and
  '**' is not supported. A pattern matching nothing is passed through
  unchanged. In cmd, quote the pattern to suppress expansion.

Examples:
  squeeze file.csv                  Compress with gzip (default)
  squeeze --zstd largefile.bin      Compress with zstd
  squeeze -d file.csv.gz            Decompress (auto-detect format)
  cat dump.sql | squeeze > dump.gz  Pipe mode compression
  squeeze --json f
